Do statistical models beat the seasonal baselines?

Rolling-origin backtest with StatsForecast.cross_validation: each window is one day ahead (h=48, step_size=48), refit on data before that day. Metrics are MAE / RMSE and skill vs seasonal naive (positive = better than "same slot yesterday"). Every window refits six models, so this takes a minute. Use fewer windows to go faster.

data.text/markdown:
Reading the result

  • A univariate model can only extrapolate the shape of recent days. Tomorrow's cloud cover is information it does not have, so a floor on error remains. That is where mlforecast with weather features, or an exogenous X_df, earns its keep.
  • AutoETS with 48 seasonal states over ~3 weeks has little data per state: expect it to overfit or lose to simple averages. MSTL sidesteps that by estimating the seasonal profile separately.
  • A smoothed seasonal average (SeasonalWindowAverage) is often the model to beat. Check whether MSTL_ARIMA justifies its extra cost.
